articles.blogTitle: Alibaba vs 1688: Which Is Better for Nigerian Importers in 2026?
articles.blogContent:
Alibaba and 1688 are two of the most important China sourcing platforms for Nigerian importers, but they are not built for the same buyer. Choosing the wrong one can raise your cost, slow your order, or expose you to supplier and payment problems.

Alibaba’s buyer guidance describes its supplier search, quotation and verification tools. Check the actual seller and order terms rather than assuming all listings offer the same protections.

This guide compares Alibaba and 1688 from a Nigerian importer's point of view: price, MOQ, supplier type, payment, communication, shipping, inspection and risk. If you need the full beginner process first, read our guide on how to import from China to Nigeria.

The short answer

Alibaba is usually easier for beginners because many suppliers communicate in English, issue export invoices and accept international payment methods. 1688 is usually better for price discovery and domestic wholesale pricing, but it is harder because it is built for Chinese buyers.

If you are buying a first test order, Alibaba may be easier. If you already understand product specifications, supplier verification and RMB payment, 1688 may give you better pricing. If you do not want to manage the process yourself, submit links through Buy From Chinese Websites.

Pricing and real cost

1688 often shows lower unit prices because it serves the domestic Chinese wholesale market. That does not automatically mean your final cost will be lower in Nigeria. You still need local China delivery, payment support, inspection, consolidation, international freight, customs and local delivery.

Alibaba prices can be higher because suppliers price for export buyers, English support, smaller trial orders and platform fees. The correct comparison is landed cost, not listed price. Use our landed cost guide and China to Nigeria shipping cost guide before deciding.

Supplier communication

Alibaba is easier if you need English conversation, quotation documents and export explanations. 1688 suppliers may reply in Chinese, expect RMB payments and assume you already understand Chinese domestic logistics.

This matters because weak communication creates wrong specifications. If a supplier cannot explain material, carton size, warranty, model differences or production time clearly, the cheaper quote can become expensive.

MOQ and product customization

Alibaba can be better for branded products and custom manufacturing because suppliers expect logo, packaging, private label and export orders. Some suppliers will support lower trial MOQs if they believe you can reorder.

1688 is strong for ready-made wholesale goods, especially fast-moving accessories and general merchandise. For deeper brand building, read how to build white label products in China.

Payment differences

Alibaba supports platform-based payments and Trade Assurance when available. That can help beginners, but only if your order details are written properly. 1688 usually requires RMB payment through Alipay, Chinese bank transfer or a procurement partner.

If you already have a confirmed supplier and only need payment help, use Pay Supplier after signing in. If you still need us to purchase from the website, use Buy From Chinese Websites.

Risk and verification

Neither platform removes risk. A verified-looking Alibaba profile can still sell poor-quality goods, and a cheap 1688 seller may not be a factory. Always verify supplier identity, product specification, production ability, reviews, business scope and inspection willingness.

Before sending money, read how to avoid scams when importing from China to Nigeria and Trading Company vs Real Manufacturer in China.

Which should you use?

Use Alibaba when you need English support, export documentation, samples, private label, custom manufacturing or a safer beginner workflow. Use 1688 when you want domestic Chinese wholesale pricing, can handle RMB payment and have a reliable partner for verification and shipping.

For phones, laptops and gadgets, do not judge by platform alone. Check grading, warranty, battery health, accessories and inspection. You can also browse available tech through the Sure Imports shop.

The best platform depends on your order type, not popularity. Alibaba is simpler. 1688 can be cheaper. The winning importer is the one who verifies the supplier, calculates landed cost and inspects before shipping.

For links from Alibaba, 1688, Taobao or other Chinese websites, start with Buy From Chinese Websites. For bulk company projects, use Corporate Sourcing.

Practical decision matrix

Choose Alibaba when you need a supplier that understands export terms, English communication, custom packaging, private label discussion, sample shipment and documentation. It is also better when you are buying technical products where explanation matters. A slightly higher unit price can be worth it if the supplier provides clearer specifications and accepts inspection.

Choose 1688 when you have exact product knowledge, can handle Chinese-language supplier communication, have RMB payment support and can consolidate goods inside China. 1688 works best when you are buying ready-made products and already know what quality level you want.

Do not use 1688 just because someone said it is cheaper. Use it when the saving remains after local delivery, payment support, inspection, freight and customs. If the saving disappears after those costs, Alibaba may be the more efficient route.

Common Nigerian buyer scenarios

If you are a beginner buying your first commercial batch, Alibaba is often easier. If you are a reseller buying repeat items such as organizers, accessories or household goods, 1688 may be stronger. If you are building a brand, start with Alibaba or direct factory sourcing. If you are buying several small products from different links, use a buying and consolidation process instead of paying suppliers one by one.

For corporate buyers, the platform matters less than specification control, branding, packaging and delivery timeline. A company buying branded gift sets or staff equipment should not be trying to save a few yuan while risking poor finishing. That type of order belongs in a scoped procurement workflow.

Final recommendation

Use Alibaba for clarity and export readiness. Use 1688 for price advantage when you have operational support. Use Sure Imports when you want the product bought, paid for, checked and moved through the process without guessing. The right platform is the one that protects your margin after the full landed cost is known.

Pre-payment checklist for either platform

Before paying on Alibaba or 1688, confirm the supplier name, product model, unit price, quantity, carton size, gross weight, production time, payment method, inspection plan and delivery address in China. If any of these details are missing, you do not yet have a complete order.

Ask for photos or videos of the actual product version you are buying. Many listings use attractive photos that do not match the low-price option. Confirm material, dimensions, accessories, packaging and any logo requirement before payment.

How to test before scaling

For a new product, start with a sample or small batch. Track defect rate, delivery cost, customer response, selling speed and actual profit. If the test works, reorder with better packaging, better carton planning and clearer inspection rules.

Do not move from first discovery to large order because the listing looks cheap. Platform choice is only the first decision. The money is made through supplier control, shipping control and Nigerian market fit.

articles.blogTitle: How To Find a Reliable Supplier in China From Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
Finding a supplier in China is easy. Finding a reliable supplier is the hard part. A Nigerian importer can get hundreds of replies from Alibaba, 1688, WeChat or referrals, but only a few suppliers will match the product quality, documentation, pricing and consistency needed for a real business.

Alibaba’s buyer guidance describes what its Verified Supplier assessment covers and where buyers can inspect the report; this badge does not replace checking the exact product and order.

This guide explains how to find and verify a reliable supplier from Nigeria before you pay. It links directly to our guides on avoiding China import scams and using a China procurement agent.

Start with a clear product brief

A vague request produces vague quotes. Write the exact product name, material, size, color, quantity, packaging, branding requirement, target market, target landed cost and acceptable quality level.

For electronics, include battery capacity, plug type, certifications, warranty expectation and test requirements. For machines, include output capacity, voltage, spare parts and raw material details. The more precise the brief, the easier it is to reject weak suppliers.

Use the right sourcing channel

Alibaba is useful for export-ready suppliers and custom manufacturing. 1688 is useful for domestic wholesale pricing. Trade fairs and referrals can be useful for serious volume buyers. WeChat is useful only when you already have a trusted contact or verification partner.

If you already have product links and want purchase support, use Buy From Chinese Websites. If the order is for a company, branded project or bulk procurement, use Corporate Sourcing.

Check whether the supplier is focused

A serious supplier usually has a clear product category. A company selling solar panels, hair, blenders, shoes and phone screens from one profile may be a general trader. General traders can help with mixed orders, but they are weaker for technical products and long-term quality control.

Ask what products they manufacture directly, what they outsource, and whether they can show current production evidence. For factories, ask for workshop videos, business license, product test reports and previous export experience.

Compare quotes properly

Do not compare only unit price. Compare MOQ, sample cost, production time, packaging, carton size, gross weight, payment terms, warranty, inspection acceptance and after-sales responsibility.

A cheaper supplier can cost more if cartons are bulky, defect rate is high or packaging fails in transit. Use our guides on CBM and volumetric weight and turning landed cost into selling price.

Verify before payment

Verification should happen before deposit. Confirm company name, bank account name, platform profile, address, business scope and whether the supplier can issue a proper invoice. Avoid sending large payments to personal accounts or unrelated names.

If your main challenge is supplier payment after verification, use Pay Supplier. If you are not sure the supplier is real, do not pay yet.

Inspect before shipping

Inspection protects your leverage. Once goods leave China, correcting mistakes becomes harder and more expensive. Inspection should confirm quantity, model, color, packaging, labels, visible defects, basic function and carton marks.

For machines, test runs matter. Read what a real China factory test run should look like before paying final balance.

A reliable supplier is not the person with the lowest quote or fastest WhatsApp reply. It is the supplier who can meet your specification, document the order, accept verification, support inspection and deliver consistent quality.

When the product is high-value, technical, branded or corporate, use a managed procurement process. That is cheaper than learning with a failed shipment.

Questions to ask before trusting a supplier

Ask whether the supplier is a factory, trading company or market wholesaler. Ask for the exact company name in Chinese and English. Ask whether the receiving account matches the company name. Ask for product videos from the current batch, not old catalog images. Ask for carton dimensions and gross weight. Ask whether third-party inspection is allowed before balance payment.

For technical goods, ask for model numbers, test reports, spare parts, voltage, plug type, warranty scope and failure handling. For branded or private label goods, ask for logo methods, packaging mockups, production lead time and minimum order quantity for custom packaging.

How to compare two suppliers that look similar

When two suppliers quote similar products, compare the hidden details. Which one explains specifications better? Which one gives carton data faster? Which one accepts inspection? Which one has a focused product range? Which one can provide sample evidence? Which one gives a written proforma invoice without pressure?

The more serious supplier is not always the cheapest. Reliability is a cost reducer because it lowers returns, delays, replacement costs and customer complaints. For Nigerian importers, those hidden costs often matter more than a small difference in supplier price.

When to walk away

Walk away when a supplier refuses basic verification, pushes personal account payment, changes account details suddenly, cannot explain product differences, avoids inspection, offers prices far below the market, or pressures you to pay immediately. Also walk away when the supplier is vague about defects, warranty or what happens if goods fail inspection.

A reliable supplier does not remove the need for process. It simply makes the process smoother. Keep written records, use clear invoices, inspect before shipping and calculate landed cost before scaling the order.

Supplier verification workflow

Use a staged process. First, shortlist suppliers from Alibaba, 1688, referrals or factory databases. Second, remove suppliers with unclear product focus, weak communication or suspicious account details. Third, request written quotes with the same specification so you can compare fairly. Fourth, verify business identity and payment details. Fifth, inspect before final shipment.

This workflow prevents emotional buying. Many importers lose money because they treat the first responsive supplier as the best supplier. Responsiveness is useful, but it is not proof of reliability.

What a good supplier response looks like

A good supplier answers the question asked, gives specific product details, explains available quality levels, provides carton information, states production time clearly and accepts reasonable inspection. They do not dodge basic questions or pressure you to pay before the order is defined.

When a supplier gives vague answers, ask once more in a structured way. If the response is still vague, move on. Your future customers in Nigeria will not care that the supplier was friendly. They will care whether the product works.

articles.blogTitle: How To Import From China Without CAC Registration in Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
Many Nigerians delay importation because they think CAC registration is required before they can buy anything from China. The answer is more practical: you can start small without CAC in many cases, but CAC becomes important as your orders, customers, documentation and business risk grow.

CAC’s company-registration guidance explains the current process; registration is separate from product-specific import and customs requirements.

This guide explains what beginners can do, when CAC matters, and how to avoid turning a simple test order into a compliance problem. For the full import workflow, read how to import from China to Nigeria.

Can you import without CAC?

For small personal purchases, samples and many mini importation orders, you can often buy and ship without having a registered company. You may buy through a procurement service, pay for goods, and receive items for resale while you test demand.

However, importing without CAC does not mean importing without responsibility. You still need correct product descriptions, safe payment, reliable shipping and awareness of restricted or regulated products.

When CAC becomes important

CAC registration becomes important when you want to open business banking relationships, supply companies, bid for corporate orders, build a formal brand, process larger shipments, access certain documentation or separate personal money from business money.

If you plan to build a long-term import business, register properly. It improves trust, accounting, invoicing and customer confidence.

Mini importation vs formal importation

Mini importation usually means smaller shipments, faster turnover and lower startup capital. Formal importation may involve larger quantities, sea freight, regulatory documents, clearing agents and more structured records.

If you are still choosing products, read the beginner guide to mini importation in Nigeria and fast-moving mini importation products.

Products that need more caution

Food, cosmetics, medical products, chemicals, electrical appliances, telecom devices and branded products can require extra documentation or approvals. CAC is only one part of compliance. Product category matters more.

Before importing regulated goods, read Nigeria customs duty on goods from China. Do not buy first and ask compliance questions after arrival.

How beginners should start

Start with a small test order, clear product specification, known selling channel and realistic landed cost. Do not borrow heavily for your first shipment. Do not buy bulky products because the supplier price looks cheap.

Use Buy From Chinese Websites if you have links and need help purchasing. If you already have a supplier and only need payment support, use Pay Supplier.

When to formalize

Formalize when customers begin asking for invoices, when you want to supply offices, when you are building a brand, when you are importing regulated products, or when monthly turnover becomes meaningful.

For company orders or branded merchandise, route the project through Corporate Sourcing so specifications, branding, timelines and compliance issues are handled from the start.

CAC registration is not always the first step, but it should not be ignored. Start lean if you must, but build records, calculate landed cost and formalize as the business proves itself.

The real mistake is not importing without CAC. The real mistake is importing without verification, documentation and cost discipline.

What you can do before CAC registration

You can research products, compare suppliers, order samples, test demand, sell small batches, build customer feedback and learn shipping costs before registering a company. This is a practical way to avoid spending money on structure before proving the market.

Keep records even if you are not yet registered. Save supplier invoices, payment receipts, shipping records, customer orders and expenses. These records help when you later formalize the business, calculate profit and understand which products deserve more capital.

What you should not do casually

Do not import regulated goods casually because you are operating small. Cosmetics, food, supplements, chemicals, medical items, branded products and some electronics can create compliance problems even when the quantity is not huge. The product category determines risk more than your CAC status.

Do not present yourself as a large formal supplier to corporate customers if you cannot invoice, document and deliver professionally. If a business customer needs official documentation, register properly or work through a structured procurement service.

A sensible growth path

Start with low-risk products, small capital, clear landed cost and a simple selling channel. After two or three successful cycles, identify your best product category. Then register the business, open better records, negotiate stronger supplier terms and consider branding.

CAC registration should follow a business model, not replace one. The goal is to move from testing to structure. Once orders become repeatable, formalization becomes an advantage rather than an administrative burden.

Documents to keep even before registration

Keep supplier invoices, payment receipts, shipping invoices, customer payment records, delivery expenses and product photos. These records help you understand profit and support later business registration, tax planning and supplier negotiation.

If you are selling through social media, keep order records in a spreadsheet. Track product cost, landed cost, selling price, delivery fee, returned items and profit per product. This discipline matters more than many beginners expect.

When CAC helps sales

CAC registration can improve trust when selling to offices, schools, churches, NGOs, retailers or corporate buyers. These customers may need invoices, receipts, account details and official communication. If you want that market, registration becomes part of your sales infrastructure.

For small consumer resale, CAC may not be urgent at the start. For corporate supply, branded products and long-term import operations, it becomes important earlier.

articles.blogTitle: How To Calculate Landed Cost Before Importing From China to Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
Supplier price is not your cost. Many Nigerian importers lose money because they buy based on the China unit price and only discover the real landed cost after shipping, customs and local delivery.

ICC’s Incoterms 2020 guidance explains how Incoterms allocate costs and risk between buyer and seller; confirm the chosen term before filling in a landed-cost worksheet.

This guide gives a practical landed cost framework. It supports our deeper guides on using the landed cost estimator and turning landed cost into a confident selling price.

What landed cost means

Landed cost is the total cost of getting a product from the supplier to the point where it is ready to sell in Nigeria. It includes the product price, China local delivery, inspection, payment charges, international freight, customs, clearing, local delivery, packaging losses and a buffer.

If you ignore any of these, your profit calculation is incomplete.

Start with product cost

Use the final negotiated unit price, not the first price on Alibaba or 1688. Confirm whether the quote includes packaging, logo, accessories, spare parts, cartons and local delivery to your China warehouse.

If the supplier changes carton size or packaging after payment, your shipping cost can change. Always ask for packing details before paying.

Add shipping cost

Shipping depends on actual weight, volumetric weight, CBM, product type, route and urgency. Small but heavy items price differently from large but light items.

Read how to calculate CBM and volumetric weight and cost of shipping from China to Nigeria before choosing air or sea freight.

Add customs and clearing

Customs cost depends on product type, value, HS code and applicable charges. Some items also need SONCAP, NAFDAC or other regulatory documentation.

Before importing, review Nigeria customs duty on goods from China. Duty is not something to guess after the goods arrive.

Add local business costs

Your landed cost should also include local delivery, warehousing, payment processing, marketplace fees, damaged units, returns, customer support and advertising if needed.

A product with a 40 percent markup can still lose money if returns, ads and delivery are ignored.

Use the selling price test

Start from the price customers in Nigeria will actually pay. Then subtract your desired profit and all costs. The remaining amount is your maximum supplier plus freight budget.

This prevents emotional buying. If the market cannot support the final price, do not import the product.

A good importer calculates landed cost before paying the supplier. A struggling importer calculates it after the goods arrive.

If you want Sure Imports to help buy products from China websites with a clearer cost view, use Buy From Chinese Websites.

Simple landed cost worksheet

Start with supplier unit price multiplied by quantity. Add China local delivery if the supplier does not deliver free to your warehouse. Add inspection or service fee if applicable. Add international shipping using either actual weight, volumetric weight or CBM depending on the method.

Then add customs duty, clearing charges, local delivery, payment charges, packaging losses, damaged stock allowance and a buffer. Divide the total by the number of sellable units, not the number of units ordered. If you expect defects, account for them before pricing.

Example thinking

If you import 500 units at a low supplier price but 20 units arrive damaged or unsellable, your cost per sellable unit increases. If the product needs ads to sell, advertising is part of the business cost. If customers often return the item, returns are part of the product economics.

This is why high-margin-looking products sometimes fail. The importer only calculated supplier price, not the actual cost of selling in Nigeria.

Decision rule before payment

Do not pay for a product until you know your estimated landed cost, realistic selling price and minimum acceptable profit. If the profit only works when everything goes perfectly, the product is risky. Exchange rate movement, shipping changes and customer returns can wipe out thin margins.

A good landed cost estimate does not need to be perfect, but it must be complete. It should show enough truth to stop you from buying products that cannot survive the Nigerian market.

Costs beginners often forget

Commonly forgotten costs include supplier bank charges, RMB payment spread, China local delivery, repacking, inspection, damaged units, local dispatch in Nigeria, marketplace commission, refunds, customer service and advertising. These may look small individually, but together they can remove profit.

Another forgotten cost is time. Slow-moving stock ties down capital. If you import a product that takes six months to sell, the profit may be weaker than a smaller-margin product that sells every week.

Use landed cost to reject products

Landed cost is not only for pricing. It is a filter. If a product cannot support freight, duty, clearing, delivery and a realistic profit, reject it before payment. This is how disciplined importers avoid dead stock.

When comparing two products, choose the one with clearer demand, lower defect risk and more predictable shipping even if the supplier price is higher. Profit is not made at purchase price alone. It is made when customers buy and stay satisfied.

articles.blogTitle: Choosing a Shipping Company From China to Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
The best shipping company from China to Nigeria is not simply the one with the cheapest rate. A cheap quote can become expensive if goods are delayed, clearing is unclear, tracking is poor or restricted products are accepted without warning.

ICC’s Incoterms 2020 guidance helps identify which party is responsible for carriage, insurance and clearance; check that your freight quote uses the same agreed terms.

This guide explains what to check before choosing a shipping company. For cost ranges and method selection, read cost of shipping from China to Nigeria.

Check what the quote includes

Ask whether the quote includes pickup in China, warehouse handling, international freight, customs clearing, terminal charges, local delivery in Nigeria and insurance. If clearing is not included, ask who handles it and what documents are required.

A quote that excludes key charges may look cheaper only because the expensive part is hidden.

Ask for air, sea and express options

Air freight is faster for smaller or higher-value goods. Sea freight works better for heavy and bulky goods. Express courier is useful for samples and urgent parcels but can be costly for resale orders.

Use air freight vs sea freight to choose based on profit, not impatience.

Verify restricted products

A serious logistics partner should warn you about batteries, liquids, powders, cosmetics, food, chemicals, branded goods, medical items and telecom devices. If a shipper accepts everything without questions, be careful.

Restricted products can create delays, extra charges or seizure risk. Review customs duty and import requirements before buying.

Demand carton details

A proper shipping quote needs carton size, gross weight, product type, number of cartons, pickup city and destination. Without these details, the quote is only a guess.

Carton optimization can improve profit. Read how carton optimization cuts shipping cost.

Look for process, not promises

Good shippers provide warehouse address, receiving process, tracking updates, expected timelines, payment records and escalation channels. They do not rely only on vague WhatsApp assurances.

If the shipment is tied to procurement, inspection and supplier payment, use a coordinated process through China procurement support.

Shipping for phones and laptops

Phones and laptops need extra care because of value, batteries, grading and theft risk. Confirm packaging, insurance options, inspection and delivery timeline.

If you want ready sourced tech, browse the Sure Imports shop. If you want us to buy from China links, use Buy From Chinese Websites.

The best shipping company is the one that gives clear costs, understands product risk, handles documentation properly and communicates before problems become expensive.

Choose logistics after you understand the product, not after goods are already sitting in a China warehouse.

Questions to ask a shipping company

Ask where their China warehouse is located, how goods are received, whether they inspect carton labels, how they calculate chargeable weight, what items they reject, how long shipping takes, and whether clearing is included. Ask what happens if goods are delayed, damaged or short-landed.

Ask for the exact destination process in Nigeria. Is pickup required? Is doorstep delivery available? Are there extra local delivery charges? Is there tracking? A vague last-mile process can frustrate customers even when international freight is fast.

Red flags

Be careful with shipping companies that quote without asking product type, weight or carton size. Be careful when they accept restricted goods without warning. Be careful when they cannot explain clearing. Be careful when they change rates after receiving goods without showing calculation.

Also be careful with timelines that sound too certain. Freight can be delayed by airline space, vessel schedules, customs checks, holidays and documentation issues. A serious shipper gives realistic windows, not magical guarantees.

How shipping affects product choice

Shipping is not a separate decision from product selection. Bulky low-value goods may look cheap in China and become weak after freight. Small high-value goods may ship well but carry theft, damage or compliance risk. Batteries, liquids and branded goods require extra caution.

Before buying, ask the shipper about the product category. The answer can determine whether the product is worth importing at all.

How to compare shipping quotes

Put quotes side by side using the same product, carton size, gross weight, pickup city and destination. Ask each company whether clearing, local delivery and handling are included. If one quote is much cheaper, find out what is excluded before choosing it.

For sea freight, confirm whether the quote is per CBM, per container, or a bundled door-to-door estimate. For air freight, confirm actual weight versus volumetric weight. For express, confirm customs handling and whether the courier will bill extra charges on arrival.

Operational discipline

Label cartons properly, keep packing lists, photograph goods before dispatch from China, and record tracking details. If multiple suppliers are sending goods to one warehouse, use clear marks so items are not mixed up.

Shipping problems are easier to solve when records are clear. Without carton marks, invoices and receiving records, disputes become guesswork.

Use a written comparison sheet

This is a selection guide, not a ranked list based on independent tests of shipping companies. Sure Imports offers shipping services, so our own service links are commercial. Obtain comparable written quotations and evaluate the provider you intend to use against the same requirements.

Ask every providerRecord in the comparison
Where does your responsibility start and end?Named pickup point, destination and handover process
How will this shipment be charged?Weight or volume basis, minimum charge, rounding and applicable divisor
What does the quote exclude?Clearance, taxes, storage, special handling, insurance and last-mile delivery
When does the transit estimate start?Warehouse receipt, booked departure or actual departure
What happens after loss or damage?Claim deadline, evidence, liability terms and insurance details
Can you accept this exact product?Written acceptance and any required documents

Compare the same chargeable shipment

Suppose the actual gross weight is 30 kg. The final packing measures 80 × 60 × 50 cm. With an assumed volumetric divisor of 6,000, dimensional weight is 40 kg. A provider using the greater of actual and dimensional weight would quote on 40 kg under that assumption. Another service may use a different divisor or minimum. Get the actual rule in writing; the example is not a rate or a universal freight formula.

A quote of “₦X per kg” is incomplete without the chargeable quantity and other fees. Ask for the total for the measured shipment. If a provider changes the packing, request the revised measurement record before approving the final invoice.

Check insurance and liability separately

Ask whether cargo insurance is included, optional or absent. If offered, obtain the policy or certificate details, covered value, exclusions, deductible and claim process. Do not assume a forwarder's liability promise provides the same cover as cargo insurance. High-value electronics, fragile goods and used goods may need particular attention to the actual terms.

Test the process with a suitable first shipment

For a new logistics relationship, start with a lawful shipment whose risk and value you can manage. Evaluate receiving acknowledgement, measurement evidence, invoice clarity, departure updates and destination handover. Keep records of discrepancies and how they were resolved. A single successful delivery does not guarantee every future shipment, but it provides more useful evidence than an unverified testimonial.

Before paying, confirm the contracting business and payment details independently. Do not send funds to a changed account solely because a message arrived in an existing chat. Select the provider whose documented scope fits the goods and delivery needs, and retain the accepted quotation with the packing list and shipment records.

articles.blogTitle: How To Import Phones From China to Nigeria Safely
articles.blogContent:
Phones are one of the most attractive import categories in Nigeria because demand is constant. They are also one of the easiest categories to lose money in if grading, battery health, parts history and supplier trust are not handled properly.

For used iPhones, Apple’s pre-owned iPhone checklist identifies Activation Lock, battery health and parts history as device-level checks to make before accepting a batch.

This guide explains how to import phones from China to Nigeria safely. If you prefer already sourced options, check the Sure Imports shop.

Decide what type of phones you want

New phones, refurbished phones, used iPhones, Android phones, parts and accessories all have different risk profiles. Do not mix them in your mind. A used iPhone business is not the same as importing sealed Android phones.

For used devices, read how to safely source second-hand iPhones and laptops from China.

Understand grading

A-grade, B-grade and C-grade can mean different things depending on the supplier. Ask for written grading standards: screen condition, housing marks, battery health, Face ID, camera, network lock, parts replacement and warranty.

Do not accept beauty photos as grading proof. Ask for sample videos or inspection reports tied to actual units.

Check battery and parts history

Battery health is a major resale factor in Nigeria. A phone with weak battery health may sell slowly or create complaints. For iPhones, confirm Face ID, True Tone where relevant, camera, charging port, speaker, network status and iCloud status.

For Android phones, check region, storage, RAM, network bands, charger type and display condition.

Verify suppliers carefully

Phone suppliers can be wholesalers, refurbishers, market traders or aggregators. Ask how they source units, whether they test every phone, what warranty they offer, and whether inspection is allowed before shipping.

Read how to avoid scams when importing from China before paying for any phone batch.

Calculate landed cost and margin

Phones have high value in small volume, so shipping may not be the biggest cost. Your risks are defects, returns, price changes, exchange rate movement and unsold models.

Use landed cost to selling price before placing a batch order. Do not buy models only because they are cheap.

Use the right buying route

If you want us to help buy phones from Chinese websites or suppliers, use Buy From Chinese Websites. If your supplier is already confirmed and you only need payment support, use Pay Supplier.

For ready products, browse the Sure Imports shop and compare with your target market.

Phone importation can work, but only when inspection and grading are treated seriously. The profit is not in buying the cheapest batch. The profit is in buying units your customers can trust.

Start small, test models, track defects and build supplier relationships slowly.

Inspection checklist for phone batches

Check model, storage, color, battery health, screen condition, touch response, camera, speaker, microphone, charging port, network lock, Face ID or fingerprint, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, iCloud or account lock, housing marks and accessories. For used iPhones, also check replaced parts warnings where relevant.

Do not accept only group photos. A batch can look clean from distance while individual units have weak batteries, dead pixels or replacement parts. For higher-value batches, inspection should be tied to serial numbers or IMEI records.

Pricing phones for Nigeria

Phone prices move quickly. A batch that looks profitable today can become average if a newer model drops or competitors flood the market. Build margin for price movement, returns and warranty handling. Do not use all your capital on one model unless you already have buyers.

Sell based on trust. Clear grading, honest battery information and reliable after-sales handling can support better margins than vague "foreign used" claims.

When not to import phones

Do not import phones if you cannot inspect them, cannot verify the supplier, do not understand model differences, or do not have a selling channel. Do not buy locked devices, unclear grades or batches with missing test records because they look cheap.

The phone business rewards knowledge. If you are not ready to manage that detail, start with available products from the shop or use a managed sourcing process.

Building a repeat phone business

A repeat phone business depends on trust. Create clear grades for your own customers, test units before sale, document battery health and explain warranty limits. Do not oversell used phones as perfect. Honest grading reduces disputes and builds repeat buyers.

Track defect patterns by supplier and model. If one supplier repeatedly sends weak batteries or repaired screens, stop buying from them even if their price is attractive. Your reputation in Nigeria is worth more than a small unit discount.

Model selection strategy

Focus on models with steady demand, available accessories and clear resale pricing. Avoid buying too many slow-moving colors, storage sizes or region-specific models. If customers in your market prefer certain iPhone or Samsung models, let demand guide stock.

Phones are capital-intensive. Spread risk across models only when you understand each model's selling speed and margin.

articles.blogTitle: Most Profitable Mini Importation Products in Nigeria Right Now
articles.blogContent:
The most profitable mini importation products are not always the trendiest products. A good mini import product must have demand, manageable shipping cost, clear selling channel, acceptable defect risk and enough margin after landed cost.

Nigeria’s foreign-trade reports provide category-level import context. They do not prove that a particular mini-import product will be profitable; validate local demand and your own landed margin.

This guide explains how to choose profitable products instead of copying random lists. For more ideas, read top fast-moving mini importation products Nigerians buy every day.

What makes a product profitable?

A profitable product is small enough to ship affordably, useful enough to sell repeatedly, simple enough to explain, durable enough to reduce returns and priced well enough to leave margin.

Avoid products that are cheap in China but bulky, fragile, regulated or hard to sell without heavy advertising.

Strong categories

Useful categories include phone accessories, laptop accessories, beauty tools, home organization, kitchen gadgets, travel accessories, fitness accessories, baby accessories, small office tools and fashion add-ons.

For tech products, connect your research with the Sure Imports shop to understand what buyers are already looking for.

Products to treat carefully

Be careful with cosmetics, food, supplements, medical devices, batteries, branded products and electrical appliances. They can be profitable, but compliance, defect and customs risk are higher.

Read customs duty and import requirements before choosing regulated goods.

Use landed cost, not supplier price

A product that costs $1 in China can become weak after freight, clearing, local delivery, ads, returns and payment charges. Calculate landed cost before ordering.

Use the landed cost estimator guide and selling price guide.

Test before scaling

Order small quantities first. Test demand, customer objections, delivery cost, defect rate and repeat purchase. Scale only when the numbers are proven.

If you have China links, use Buy From Chinese Websites to purchase. If the order is for staff gifts, event packs or branded items, use Corporate Sourcing.

Do not ignore differentiation

The easiest way to lose margin is to sell the same product as everyone else with no packaging, bundle, content angle or customer trust. Improve presentation, bundle related items and choose a niche buyer.

White label products can help once demand is proven. Read how to build your own white label products in China.

Profitable mini importation is not guessing. It is product selection, landed cost control, supplier verification and market testing.

Start with products you can understand, sell and support. Then scale with data, not excitement.

Product selection scorecard

Score every product on demand, shipping weight, fragility, defect risk, regulation risk, competition, repeat purchase, ease of explanation and margin. A product with medium demand but low shipping cost and low defect rate can be better than a viral product with high returns.

Do not ignore customer education. If buyers do not immediately understand why they need the product, you may need content, demos and ads. That raises your selling cost.

Examples of safer mini import products

Safer categories often include phone stands, laptop stands, cable organizers, storage bags, compact kitchen tools, travel organizers, beauty accessories that are not regulated cosmetics, small fitness accessories, desk accessories and simple household problem-solvers.

Riskier categories include skincare formulas, supplements, rechargeable devices with weak quality control, fragile glass items, bulky furniture, counterfeit branded goods and products that require complex after-sales support.

How to scale winners

Once a product sells well, improve the offer before simply buying more. Better packaging, bundles, clearer instructions, warranty cards, branded inserts and better product photos can increase perceived value. When demand is proven, consider white labeling or sourcing a better version.

The goal is not to import every trending product. The goal is to build repeatable product lines with known suppliers, known costs and predictable customers.

Where beginners should sell first

Start with channels you can manage: WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, small retail partnerships, marketplaces or community groups. Do not import a product before knowing where the first 30 to 50 buyers may come from.

Validate with content before buying heavily. Post product demos, ask for pre-orders, compare prices and watch comments. Demand signals are not perfect, but they are better than importing blindly.

Inventory discipline

Keep stock records. Know how many units were bought, sold, returned, damaged and remaining. Many small importers confuse sales with profit because cash is moving. Inventory records show the truth.

When a product sells, reorder before stock is completely gone, but do not over-order until demand is repeatable. The best mini importation businesses manage cash flow as carefully as product sourcing.

articles.blogTitle: Bulk Laptop Sourcing From China for Nigerian Businesses: What To Specify Before You Pay
articles.blogContent:
Bulk laptop sourcing is one of the easiest procurement categories to get wrong. Two laptops can have the same brand name and look similar in photos, yet differ in processor generation, RAM, storage type, battery condition, screen quality, keyboard layout, grade and real business usefulness. For Nigerian companies, schools, training centres, NGOs and teams, the cost of wrong specification is not only financial. It affects productivity.

Intel’s processor-identification guide shows why “Core i5” alone is not a complete specification; record the full processor model and generation for every proposed laptop batch.

This guide supports how to import laptops from China to Nigeria safely and the page for laptops for businesses. If you need a managed procurement route for company laptops, do not treat it as a casual website order. Use Corporate Sourcing or the dedicated business laptop page so the requirement is specified properly.

Define the real use case first

A laptop for data entry is not the same as a laptop for design, software development, video editing, accounting, call centre work or AI training. Before asking for prices, define what the laptops must do. List the applications, expected workload, user type, mobility needs, battery expectations and whether the devices will be used in one office or distributed across locations.

This prevents false savings. A cheaper machine that cannot run the required tools is not cheaper. It becomes downtime, complaints, replacement cost and procurement embarrassment. Start from function, then match specifications.

Specify processor generation, not only Core i5 or Core i7

Many buyers ask for Core i5 or Core i7 without stating generation. That is a serious mistake. A newer Core i5 can outperform an older Core i7. Ask for processor model and generation. Also specify minimum RAM, storage size, whether storage is SSD or HDD, screen size, resolution expectation and whether upgrade options matter.

For business use, SSD storage is usually important because it affects speed. RAM should match workload. If staff will use browsers, spreadsheets, video calls and business applications at the same time, underpowered machines will slow the team down.

Understand grade and condition language

If buying used, refurbished or open-box laptops, grade language matters. Grade A, B or C can mean different things depending on supplier. Ask what each grade allows: scratches, dents, screen marks, keyboard wear, battery health, charger condition and warranty position. Do not accept grade language without examples.

Request real photos or videos of sample units, not only catalogue photos. If possible, request a sample or inspection evidence before bulk release. For large orders, a small inspection cost can prevent a large procurement mistake.

Battery, keyboard and charger details are not minor

Battery condition affects user experience immediately. Keyboard layout affects usability. Charger quality affects safety and reliability. Nigerian businesses should specify acceptable battery health or backup expectation, keyboard preference and charger condition. If replacement chargers are included, ask whether they are original, compatible or third-party.

For teams, standardization matters. A mixed batch with inconsistent chargers, keyboards and battery performance can create support issues. It may still be acceptable if priced correctly, but it should be a deliberate decision, not a surprise.

Calculate total cost per usable device

Do not judge only supplier price per laptop. Calculate total cost per usable device after shipping, duty, clearing, local delivery, possible repairs and expected replacement rate. Use the Landed Cost Estimator and compare shipping with the Air vs Sea Calculator.

If the order is urgent for onboarding, training or project launch, timing may be more important than the lowest freight option. Read China to Nigeria shipping, Customs and landed cost before choosing logistics.

A procurement checklist for business laptops

  • Use case and required applications documented.
  • Processor model and generation specified.
  • Minimum RAM, SSD size and screen size agreed.
  • Grade, battery, keyboard and charger condition clarified.
  • Sample, photos, video or inspection evidence requested.
  • Landed cost per usable device calculated.
  • Procurement record saved in your Sure Imports account.

Approve a batch specification, not a laptop description

Build a line-item specification before asking for a bulk quote. Include manufacturer and model family, processor generation and exact processor, memory, storage type and capacity, screen size and resolution, ports, wireless hardware and operating-system requirements. Write any permitted substitutions beside the original item. “Core i5, 8 GB RAM” spans machines with materially different age and usefulness.

Set a measurable condition standard. For used or refurbished machines, agree how cosmetic grades are defined, which faults are excluded and what battery-health evidence will be supplied. Specify the keyboard layout, charger wattage, plug arrangement and whether a working original or compatible charger is included. Ask how each device will be labelled so a failed unit can be traced back to its batch and seller.

Test a sample against the tasks employees actually perform, including calls, browser-based tools and any specialist software. A successful boot is only the first check. Confirm the ports, camera, keyboard, screen, wireless connection, storage health and battery behaviour. If the sample passes, keep its recorded specification as the reference for the shipment inspection.

For inspection, agree a sampling plan and rejection rule before the goods are packed. Define which defects require replacement, repair, credit or rejection of the batch. Record serial numbers or other identifiers where available. A photograph of sealed cartons cannot show whether the machines inside match the processor, battery and charger terms you approved.

Calculate cost per usable laptop rather than only cost per unit shipped. Include freight, clearing, local delivery, expected replacements and setup work, using your own measured failure allowance where possible. A lower price can be false economy if the team loses working days replacing chargers, batteries or unusable devices. Put acceptance and after-sales responsibilities in the purchase order.

The landed cost estimator can help structure the cost comparison. For a specified corporate batch, corporate sourcing is the appropriate route to discuss samples, inspection and delivery. The laptop import guide covers the wider import steps; your batch sheet should remain the document that determines what can be accepted.

articles.blogTitle: How Nigerian Wholesalers Can Build Repeat Supply Lines From China
articles.blogContent:
A wholesaler does not win by importing once. A wholesaler wins by building repeat supply. The first order proves that a product can move. The second and third orders prove whether the supplier, packaging, landed cost, shipping route and customer demand can become a system. Nigerian wholesalers who treat every order as a fresh gamble will struggle to compound their advantage.

ICC’s Incoterms 2020 guidance can help keep freight responsibilities consistent between repeat orders; record the agreed term alongside each supplier quote.

This guide is for retailers, market sellers, online vendors, distributors and business owners who want a stronger China to Nigeria supply system. It connects to the pillar on importing from China to Nigeria and the product research guide on profitable mini importation products in Nigeria.

Separate product testing from supply building

The first order should answer whether the product can sell. Keep it controlled. Do not overbuy because the supplier price looks attractive. Test demand, customer feedback, delivery speed, defect rate, packaging and actual profit. If the first order works, the second order should improve the system rather than merely repeat it.

Supply building starts when you document what worked. Which supplier delivered? Which variant sold fastest? Which colour was slow? What was the final landed cost? What complaints came from customers? What shipping method protected margin? Without this data, the next order is just another guess.

Build a preferred supplier file

Your supplier file should include supplier name, platform link, contact, product links, quote history, payment terms, carton data, defect notes and repeat-order performance. If the supplier improves over time, keep them close. If quality declines, record it and compare alternatives before the next payment.

For supplier selection, use how to find a reliable supplier in China from Nigeria and the supplier verification checklist. If the product becomes important to your business, consider Corporate Sourcing to find stronger supply options or negotiate better structure.

Standardize specifications

Repeat orders fail when specifications are loose. If customers liked a specific size, colour, material, grade or packaging, write it down. The supplier should not choose for you on the next order. Standardization also helps staff, partners or procurement agents buy correctly when you are not personally handling every detail.

For products with variants, create your own SKU names. This makes inventory and reorder decisions easier. A supplier's product title may change, but your internal SKU should remain stable.

Use landed cost history to protect margin

Margins change because exchange rates, shipping rates, duty assumptions and supplier prices change. Keep landed cost history for each order. Use the Landed Cost Estimator every time, not only on the first order. Use the Retail Price Builder when naira costs shift.

If a product's margin is shrinking, do not ignore it. You may need to increase price, change quantity, improve packaging, switch supplier, move from air to sea, or stop importing that product. Good wholesalers are disciplined about numbers.

Use shipping strategy as a competitive advantage

Many wholesalers choose shipping by habit. Better wholesalers compare route, speed, volume and cash flow. Air freight may help you restock fast and protect sales momentum. Sea freight may help you reduce cost on bulky repeat goods. Use the Air vs Sea Calculator and read China to Nigeria shipping, Customs and landed cost.

For goods already with suppliers, use Ship With Us. But make sure your supplier sends accurate carton data and tracking details. A messy supplier handover slows everything down.

Turn repeat supply into business assets

A reliable supplier list, landed cost history, product performance record and reorder system are business assets. They make your business more predictable. They also make it easier to hire help, raise working capital, plan stock and negotiate with customers.

If you are moving from small importation to wholesale or corporate supply, create a free Sure Imports account and keep your buying, supplier payment and shipping activity organized. The goal is not only to import. The goal is to build a supply machine that can survive pressure.

Repeat supply checklist

  • Test product demand before scaling quantity.
  • Save supplier and product records after every order.
  • Standardize SKUs, variants and specifications.
  • Track landed cost history and margin movement.
  • Compare air and sea based on cash flow and volume.
  • Use sourcing support when a product becomes strategic.
  • Keep all order evidence in one business file.

Manage the second order as carefully as the first

A successful test shipment is the beginning of a supply record, not proof that every later batch will be identical. Record the exact product specification, packaging, approved sample, supplier contact, delivery term, landed cost and defect findings from the first order. Give the specification a version number. When you reorder, the supplier should confirm that version or identify each proposed change in writing.

Set a reorder trigger based on sales and lead time. Note how many units sell in a typical period, how long production and shipping took on actual orders, and how much stock you need while the next shipment is in transit. Keep a reserve for delays without treating every slow-moving variant as essential stock. The trigger should be reviewed when demand or shipping conditions change.

Track landed cost by SKU and batch. Include domestic movement in China, freight, clearing, local delivery and damaged or rejected units. Compare the new quotation with the last paid order, not only with a marketplace price. If the supplier changes the minimum quantity, carton size or payment schedule, recalculate the cash tied up and the selling margin before approving the reorder.

Use a short incoming-goods check each time. Compare the received quantity, materials, colour, dimensions, labels and packaging with the approved version. Photograph deviations and record the supplier's remedy. A repeated supplier relationship should make discrepancies easier to resolve because both sides have a clear reference, not because the buyer stops inspecting.

Keep an alternative supplier or product plan for critical stock, but do not call two listings interchangeable until their specifications and samples have been compared. If the primary supplier cannot meet the schedule, decide whether the substitute is acceptable to your customers and what extra cost it creates. Record the decision so the next buyer does not unknowingly repeat a failed substitution.

Review the supply line after every completed shipment: time from purchase order to receipt, units accepted, final landed cost, sales speed and customer complaints. Use those facts to refine the next order. The shipping and landed-cost guide explains the wider cost structure; corporate sourcing can help when repeat specifications and supplier coordination need more formal control. A reliable supply line is a sequence of documented, checked orders.

articles.blogTitle: China Imports and Stock Turnover for Nigerian Retailers
articles.blogContent:
Retailers do not only need profitable products. They need products that turn. Slow stock ties down cash, fills shelves, reduces flexibility and forces discounting. China imports can improve stock turnover when retailers buy around demand, landed cost, replenishment speed and repeat supply instead of chasing random cheap products.

Shopify’s inventory-turnover guide explains the cost-of-goods-sold and average-inventory calculation; use your own sales records to compare replenishment cycles.

This guide is for Nigerian retailers, online vendors, boutique owners, gadget sellers, market sellers and small distributors. It builds on How Nigerian Wholesalers Can Build Repeat Supply Lines From China and How To Choose Products To Import From China for the Nigerian Market.

Start with sales velocity

Before importing, look at what already moves. Which products sell weekly? Which variants move fastest? Which price points customers accept without long negotiation? Which items create repeat visits? Stock turnover improves when import decisions are tied to sales evidence.

Do not overbuy a product because the supplier gives a discount at higher quantity. A discount that creates dead stock is not a discount. Test first, then scale the variants that move.

Use landed cost to set reorder rules

A retailer should know the landed cost and selling price of each imported item. Use the Landed Cost Estimator and Retail Price Builder before the order arrives. If margin is too thin, you will struggle to discount or absorb losses.

Keep a reorder sheet with supplier link, last landed cost, selling price, quantity sold, slow variants and customer complaints. This turns importation into retail management, not guesswork.

Balance fast restock and low freight cost

Air freight can protect fast-moving stock when the margin supports it. Sea freight can protect cost for planned bulk replenishment. Retailers should use both intelligently. Use Air vs Sea Calculator and read Air Freight From China to Nigeria and Sea Shipping From China to Nigeria.

The goal is not always the cheapest shipping. The goal is the right stock at the right time with margin intact. A fast-moving product that is out of stock too long creates lost sales.

Improve product mix over time

Every order should teach you something. Remove weak colours, add stronger variants, improve packaging, negotiate better supplier terms and build repeat supply for winners. Use Corporate Sourcing when a product becomes strategic and needs a better supplier than the first link you found.

Use Buy From Chinese Websites for simple link purchases and create a free Sure Imports account so repeat orders are easier to manage.

Use a reorder point that includes goods already on the way

A practical starting calculation is expected demand during replenishment time plus safety stock. If a product sells 10 units a week, replenishment takes eight weeks and you deliberately allow 20 units of safety stock, the illustrative reorder point is 100 units. Review this against your actual variability; it is not a universal buffer.

Compare that point with inventory position: saleable stock on hand plus confirmed incoming stock, less units already committed to customers. With 45 on hand, 80 in transit and 15 committed, the position is 110. Looking only at the 45 on the shelf could trigger an unnecessary order. Keep damaged stock and unconfirmed supplier promises out of available inventory.

Measure stock turnover and sell-through separately

Inventory turnover for a period is cost of goods sold divided by average inventory valued at cost. If cost of goods sold is ₦1.2 million and average inventory is ₦400,000, turnover is three times for that period. Do not divide sales revenue by inventory cost and call the result the same measure. Also do not compare a monthly figure with an annual figure without adjusting the period.

Sell-through is useful for an individual purchase: of the units available in a batch, how many were sold during the review period? Track it by variant. A strong overall rate can conceal unpopular colours or sizes. Returns should reduce net units sold, and stockouts should be recorded because sales during a stockout do not reveal the demand you missed.

Choose a replenishment method for each item

Demand patternBuying approach to evaluateMain risk
Stable repeat salesPlanned replenishment against measured lead timeSupplier or shipping delays
New style with little evidenceSmall test quantity with a fixed review dateOverestimating demand
Seasonal demandOrder against the last useful arrival dateStock arriving after the selling window
Slow but necessary spare partLow stock with a service-based justificationMisreading low turnover as automatically unprofitable

Decide what to do with ageing inventory

Give slow stock an owner and a deadline. Check whether the problem is visibility, pricing, an incorrect specification or genuinely weak demand. Improve the listing only where the product itself is suitable. If discounting is necessary, model cash recovered after selling costs rather than defending the original target margin indefinitely.

Do not bundle an unsafe or defective item merely to clear inventory. Record the reason for each write-off or return and feed it into the next supplier brief. A useful monthly review ends with specific changes: reorder fewer pink units, stop a failing model, reserve cash for the reliable cable, or shorten a supplier's acceptable delivery window.

articles.blogTitle: Bags and Backpacks in Nigeria: Import Rules and Buying Checks
articles.blogContent:
Before sourcing bags or backpacks for Nigerian customers, establish whether the exact goods can lawfully be imported. This guide starts with that restriction, then explains how to evaluate bags from lawful local or other approved sources.

For the shipping and customs steps behind the bag quote, use China to Nigeria Shipping, Customs and Landed Cost: The Pillar Guide.

Confirm the legal route before requesting bag samples

Nigeria's official trade portal lists bags and suitcases under import prohibitions, with specified HS-code ranges. Do not treat a backpack, handbag or branded event bag as a routine permissible import simply because it is available on a Chinese marketplace. Obtain current classification and eligibility confirmation for the exact item from the relevant authority before paying.

A forwarding quote does not establish an exemption. Neither does a supplier's suggestion to describe the goods differently. Use an accurate description, material and intended use. Where the proposed goods are prohibited, use Nigerian production or lawful local supply. Do not attempt to solve a restriction by mislabelling the shipment. The quality checks in this guide are also useful when evaluating local manufacturers and existing local stock.

Write a specification that fits the user

For a laptop bag, measure the intended device and identify whether the compartment needs additional space for a sleeve. For a school bag, consider the intended age group and obtain appropriate safety and suitability advice. For an event tote, define the actual contents and whether the recipient needs to reuse it. “Large” or “premium” is not a measurable requirement.

SpecificationWhat to record
DimensionsExternal size and usable compartment dimensions
MaterialOuter fabric, lining, padding and any coating
ConstructionSeams, reinforcement points, strap attachment and edge finishing
ClosuresZipper or fastener specification and replacement availability
BrandingApproved artwork, size, placement and decoration method
PackingProtection against deformation, scuffing and moisture

Evaluate a representative sample

Inspect stitching around handles, straps and corners, because these points experience repeated stress. Check whether lining catches in the zipper and whether pockets fit the objects they are meant to hold. Have an appropriate professional define any load or durability testing needed for the intended use. A brief hand pull is not evidence of a safe carrying capacity.

View the sample in ordinary daylight and compare it with the agreed material and colour references. Check printing and embroidery on the actual fabric. A digital mockup cannot show puckering, thread quality or how a logo behaves on a curved pocket. Keep the approved sample and require approval before material substitutions.

Compare local quotations on accepted units

For an illustrative local order of 200 bags costing ₦800,000 delivered, ten unacceptable units would raise the purchase cost per accepted bag from ₦4,000 to about ₦4,211. Add any agreed repair, packaging and distribution costs. Ask whether the supplier will replace rejects and on what schedule. These figures demonstrate the comparison method; they are not a bag-price estimate.

For bulk distribution, label cartons by colour, size or recipient group and reconcile quantities before the distribution date. Record complaints by failure type so a future order can improve the construction. The purchasing decision should start with lawful availability and end with an accepted product that suits its user, not with the lowest overseas listing price.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: How Sure Imports Affiliate Tracking and Attribution Work
articles.blogContent:
Affiliate tracking and attribution answer two different questions: what interaction was recorded, and which affiliate owns an eligible commercial outcome. For Sure Imports, a visit is not the final outcome. Attribution must connect a partner’s introduction to the relevant paid service event.

After understanding attribution, read Sure Imports Affiliate Commission Rates and How Earnings Are Calculated.

Understanding that chain helps affiliates troubleshoot responsibly. It also prevents the common mistake of treating every click, request estimate or customer registration as earned commission.

The attribution chain

  1. The affiliate selects the correct service link or approved API workflow.
  2. A customer uses that route and the platform records the relevant referral context.
  3. The customer starts the intended service journey.
  4. A qualifying payment or fully paid linked invoice occurs.
  5. The system applies the configured commission basis and creates a snapshot.
  6. The commission passes through the review workflow before becoming available.

Why a click is not a commission

Clicks reveal interest, but some visitors are researching, some abandon the process and some choose an ineligible service. Commission exists only after the configured business outcome. That design aligns the programme with delivered customer value rather than raw advertising volume.

Use click and visit data to improve content, but use attributed eligible transactions to evaluate commercial performance. A page with fewer visitors can be more valuable if it answers a high-intent question precisely.

Service-specific qualifying events

Buy From Chinese Websites uses eligible product cost. Supplier Reports, Phones and Laptops, and Supplier Verification use fixed eligible transactions. Supplier Intelligence uses qualifying subscription payments. Ship with Us waits for the linked invoice to be fully paid and uses final eligible billed quantity.

These distinctions explain why two referrals that begin on the same day may appear in different stages. One might be awaiting payment, another under review and another available.

API request ownership

When an authorised affiliate API key creates a shipping request and the API accepts it, that affiliate owns the request. The creation response includes attribution details and a lock time. Retries with the same idempotency key should resolve to the same logical creation instead of producing competing requests.

Request ownership is deliberately narrower than the customer’s general relationship. It does not rewrite attribution for unrelated services or future journeys. This gives business integrations certainty about requests they originate without claiming every action that customer may ever take.

How to reduce lost or disputed attribution

  • Use the service link copied from your authenticated dashboard, not a manually edited approximation.
  • Test the link in a clean browser and confirm that it reaches the intended service journey.
  • Do not place another partner’s tracking parameters inside your content.
  • For API requests, retain the external reference, idempotency key and returned request ID.
  • Do not ask customers to create duplicates when a request already exists.
  • Raise a support query with specific references and timestamps, never with an unsupported earnings estimate.

Privacy-aware measurement

Attribution does not justify collecting more personal data than necessary. Dashboard reports can identify operational outcomes while masking customer details where appropriate. Affiliates should protect exports and avoid sharing customer records in public communities.

For content analytics, track aggregate landing-page and conversion patterns. For transaction support, use the identifiers supplied by the platform. This separation keeps marketing analysis useful without turning customer data into promotional material.

A practical reconciliation routine

Once a week, compare your published service links, attributed requests, commission statuses and completed payouts. Annotate campaigns with dates and topics so you can explain changes. For API integrations, reconcile your external reference against the Sure Imports request ID.

If traffic rises but attributed requests do not, inspect link placement and intent. If requests rise but eligible payments do not, improve qualification and explain the service more accurately. If a status changes after payment, check review and reversal information before escalating.

The practical next step

Treat tracking as an evidence chain. Preserve clean links and request identifiers, explain the qualifying event accurately, and reconcile dashboard stages instead of estimating commission from traffic.

Frequently asked questions

Does every tracked visit create commission?

No. A customer must complete the qualifying paid event for an eligible service.

Is an API-created shipping request permanently attributed?

The accepted request has locked affiliate ownership. This request-level ownership does not replace the customer’s general relationship for unrelated journeys.

What should a business store after API creation?

Store its external reference, idempotency key, returned request ID, status and attribution record.

Why can commission change during review?

Refunds, reversals, duplication, eligibility issues or breaches can affect pending commission.

How do I troubleshoot attribution?

Verify the exact link or API identifiers, note timestamps and service route, then use those records when contacting support.

articles.blogTitle: Sure Imports Affiliate Payouts: Review Periods, Balances and Withdrawals
articles.blogContent:
Sure Imports affiliate payouts begin long before a withdrawal request. A transaction must first be attributed, paid, calculated on its eligible basis and reviewed. The dashboard separates these stages so affiliates can distinguish potential commission from funds that are actually available.

If a balance is still under review, first check How Sure Imports Affiliate Tracking and Attribution Work.

The current configured review period for eligible services is 14 days as verified on 11 September 2026. A review period is not a promise that every pending entry will be approved; the transaction must remain eligible under the current terms.

Understand each balance state

StateWhat it generally meansHow to treat it
Tracked or requestedA referral interaction or service request existsOperational signal, not earnings
Pending or in reviewA commission snapshot exists but checks remainDo not count as withdrawable cash
AvailableThe commission has satisfied the applicable review workflowUse for payout planning
PaidA payout record has been completedReconcile with the destination account
Reversed or rejectedEligibility did not survive review or changed laterRead the reason and update records

Why the 14-day review exists

Cross-border services can involve payment reversals, refunds, duplicated requests, invoice corrections and service cancellations. The review window gives the programme time to verify that commission was calculated on a completed eligible event and not on an excluded or temporary amount.

A shipping estimate can also differ from the final billed quantity. The commission snapshot uses the final eligible KG or CBM after full invoice payment, not the quantity typed into the first request.

Prepare payout details carefully

Use accurate account-holder and payment details in the dashboard. A mismatch can delay or fail a transfer. Keep your affiliate profile current, follow any identity or tax-information request that applies, and never send sensitive payment credentials through public comments or community chats.

Where the dashboard supports different currencies or payout methods, follow the options made available to your account. A commission denominated in one currency should not be assumed to convert at a rate chosen by the affiliate.

Reconcile a payout

  1. Record the payout reference, date, amount and currency shown in the affiliate dashboard.
  2. Compare it with the receiving account and allow for the stated processing route.
  3. Keep pending commission separate from available commission in your own forecast.
  4. Map reversals or adjustments to the underlying transaction reference.
  5. Contact support with exact references if a completed payout does not arrive as expected.

Common reasons commission may not become available

The customer may not have paid, the service or invoice line may be excluded, the transaction may be duplicated or self-referred in breach of the terms, or a payment may have been refunded or reversed. A service request can also remain operationally active without yet creating a commission event.

The best first step is to inspect status and transaction details rather than infer a system error from a click count. If the record appears inconsistent, provide the affiliate support team with the service, request or transaction reference and relevant date.

Plan cash flow conservatively

Do not commit pending commission to advertising costs, staff bonuses or partner shares before it becomes available. Use a rolling forecast with separate columns for pending, expected review date, available and paid. Apply a conservative adjustment until you have enough history to understand your own approval pattern.

A sustainable affiliate business measures net available and paid commission after content and promotion costs. Gross dashboard activity can look impressive while producing little actual margin if acquisition is expensive or traffic is poorly qualified.

The practical next step

Keep accurate payout details, learn the dashboard states and reconcile by transaction reference. Base spending decisions on available and paid commission, not clicks, requests or pending balances.

The current configured period is 14 days for the eligible services documented in this series.

Can a pending commission be reversed?

Yes. Refunds, reversals, duplication, ineligibility or terms violations can affect a pending entry.

Is a shipping request immediately payable?

No. Commission depends on a fully paid linked invoice and the final eligible billable quantity, followed by review.

What information should I keep for reconciliation?

Keep transaction or request references, dates, amounts, currencies, statuses and payout references.

Where do I request or monitor payouts?

Use the authenticated affiliate dashboard and the payout options available to your account.
